notes: Seventh sweep (2026-10-31, head 0814e8d, uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript carries the tier's model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (tool calls are Read on the input file, Write, Edit and Bash), no transcript mentions SKILL.md, ex_unit.md or processes.md, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line (Do not invoke any skills.) requires; skills_listed is 209. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the eleven rules this case's index rows name, four changed or are new, and three of them (do:, One expression, pipelines) were added to this case's row since the 2026-10-23 sweep, which graded eight. "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" is new. "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" is rewritten. "Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" has a rewritten first bullet and an example. In ex_unit.md, "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" adds one sentence on condition blocks. The other seven are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard, using the 2026-10-29-check and 2026-10-31-check gradings where 2026-10-23 had no shape (the receive do: form, membership checks, bare matches inside private helpers).

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (changed): 2 of 5 violate (sonnet-1, sonnet-2). The deciding sentence is "A body of several sequential expressions, or one that holds a construct with a structure of its own, a `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`, a comment, or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is": sonnet-1 line 189 pid = spawn(fn -> receive do: (:crash -> exit(:boom)) end) and sonnet-2 line 227 pid = spawn(fn -> receive do: (:stop -> :ok) end) write a receive on do:, its body a -> clause, the shape 2026-10-29-check graded violated. Clean constructs: opus-1 line 288 defp await_publish(server), do: :sys.get_state(server) and sonnet-2 line 36 defp nil_name, do: :"subscriptions_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}", decided by "A `do:` body is one expression on the head's line: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not."; opus-1 line 19 if to == "bounce@example.com", do: {:error, :bounced}, else: :ok, decided by "`if ..., do: ..., else: ...` stays on one line while its condition and both branches are plain" (both branches are literals, neither computes); sonnet-2's two for loops (lines 102-113, 117-119) are do ... end, per "A `for` always takes `do ... end`". haiku-1 and haiku-2 have no do: at all and write every body holding a fn or receive as a block (haiku-1 204-206, 209-219; haiku-2 172-186), graded clean as 2026-10-31-check graded such files.

"One expression per line, and tabular clauses" (new): 2 of 5 violate (sonnet-1, sonnet-2), on the same lines as the do: rule. The deciding sentence is "A `fn` reads the same way: `fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end` holds a pattern and one expression and stays on one line, and a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes on the lines after the `->`.": sonnet-1 line 189 and sonnet-2 line 227 put a receive, a nested construct the first paragraph names, on the fn's line. Clean constructs, decided by "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces.": one-expression do: heads (opus-1 288, sonnet-2 36); single-clause receives with one expression (haiku-2 175 :stop -> :ok and 183 msg -> send(parent, {:forwarded, self(), msg}), sonnet-1 33, sonnet-2 107); sonnet-2 lines 17-18 nil -> :ok / sink -> send(sink, {:delivered, to, subject}), two simple clauses; one-line fns with one expression (haiku-1 153, 205; sonnet-1 172; sonnet-2 39, 197); every fn holding a receive in opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 puts it below its head, per "Those go on the lines below the head"; every test, setup and helper with several steps has them below its head. sonnet-1 lines 40-41 (cond: fun.() -> :ok / attempts == 0 -> flunk("condition not met in time")) each hold one condition and one expression, which this rule's first paragraph allows; the mixed layout beside the block clause at 42-44 is decided by the -> rule and the formatter, so it is listed outside the case's rules. sonnet-2 lines 245-246 are a head mix format spread because the test name is long; one selection with its body below, not counted, as 2026-10-31-check did.

"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" (changed in its first bullet): 1 of 5 violates. sonnet-1 line 22 server = start_supervised!({Subscriptions, mailer: TestMailer, name: nil} |> child_spec()) is decided by the unchanged bullet "Do not pipe a single step: write `String.trim(name)`, not `name |> String.trim()`."; the changed sentence "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short" is about two or more steps and has nothing to apply to, since this is the only |> in the five files. The other four have no |> and are not exercised.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (changed in its describe half): 5 of 5 violate, from 4 in 2026-10-23. The new sentence "A block named after a condition, or after a requirement where the project asks for that, still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict: `describe "an update survives encoding and applying"`, not `describe "the round trip"`, which names a topic and promises nothing." decides opus-1 line 54 describe "the default server" do, a noun phrase like "the round trip" over tests of subscribe/2, subscribers/1 and publish/2; this is opus-1's only violation of the rule, and without the new sentence it would be clean as in 2026-10-23. The unchanged sentence on two-function blocks decides the other four: describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2" at haiku-1 line 51, haiku-2 line 33, sonnet-1 line 55, sonnet-2 line 56. Test names breaking the unchanged test-name sentence: haiku-1 line 120 "returns :ok when the topic has no subscribers"; sonnet-1 line 94 "returns :ok even with no subscribers"; sonnet-2 line 57 "returns :ok" and line 134 "publishing to a topic with no subscribers is fine" ("is fine" says only that the call did not fail, like "works"). Clean: every "when a subscribed process exits" (opus-1 199, haiku-2 95, sonnet-1 163, sonnet-2 189) and haiku-1 146 "when a subscribed pid exits", which name the situation the rule's own ExUnit example names; function-plus-condition blocks (opus-1 "publish/3 to processes", "publish/3 to email addresses"; haiku-1 "publish/3 to pid subscribers", "publish/3 to email subscribers"; sonnet-2 "publish/3 to process subscribers", "publish/3 to email subscribers"). haiku-1 line 52 "returns :ok and lists a subscribed pid" names an effect beside :ok, clean as 2026-10-31-check held the same shape. Not counted, as in earlier grades: "requires the :mailer option" (haiku-1 42, sonnet-1 49), "keeps running when the mailer returns an error" (haiku-2 83), "the server keeps running" (sonnet-1 214), "does nothing on a topic with no subscribers" (opus-1 148), "handles pid and email subscribers on the same topic" (sonnet-2 178, its body asserts both deliveries).

"Assert with patterns" (unchanged): 4 of 5 violate. Bare matches in test bodies, counted as in 2026-10-23 (a literal, tuple, list or map on the left, without assert, inside a test block): opus-1 28 (lines 76, 77, 89, 90, 91, 98, 99, 109, 119, 120, 129, 140, 158, 159, 168, 169, 178, 188, 189, 202, 211, 221, 222, 232, 233, 254, 255, 256); haiku-2 26 (lines 35, 36, 42, 50, 51, 58, 59, 60, 67, 68, 77, 78, 86, 87, 98, 107, 116, 117, 127, 128, 134, 140, 141, 153, 161, 165); haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 0. Two judgment calls decide the other violations, both by the earlier treatment of predicate assertions: haiku-1 line 37 assert Process.whereis(Subscriptions) != nil is the is_pid(Process.whereis(...)) check 2026-10-21, 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 graded violated, spelled with != nil; sonnet-2 line 121 assert length(pids) == 3 is the construct 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 listed with is_pid in their violation evidence, and here it is the only evidence, so sonnet-2 is clean if that ruling goes the other way. sonnet-1 line 168 assert pid in Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") is a membership check, clean as 2026-10-23 skill and 2026-10-31-check held. No run uses elem/2, puts the expected value on the left of ==, or binds a held value and compares it with == afterwards; opus-1 line 33 assert Process.whereis(Subscriptions) == server has the value under test on the left.

"Wait for messages, not for time" (unchanged): 5 of 5 violate, as in 2026-10-23. Process.sleep polling after exits: opus-1 line 296, haiku-1 line 239, haiku-2 line 201, sonnet-1 line 43, sonnet-2 line 48. :DOWN patterns: opus-1 line 244 :killed (before subscribing, not after an exit under test); haiku-1 line 225 _reason (helper kill_and_wait/1); haiku-2 line 151 _reason; sonnet-1 line 194 :boom and line 238 _ (helper stop/1); sonnet-2 line 238 _. opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 never monitor a subscriber whose exit is under test. One-shot assert Process.alive? (opus-1 216, haiku-1 122, haiku-2 91, sonnet-1 221, sonnet-2 256) is not polling and is not counted. Sync calls before refute_received are present in every run (opus-1 :sys.get_state at 288; haiku-1 a second publish at 114; haiku-2 line 71; sonnet-1 line 145; sonnet-2 lines 129 and 173).

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" (unchanged): 4 of 5 violate. opus-1 line 28 starts every test's server under the default global name Notify.Subscriptions (no :name), graded violated as 2026-10-23 graded the same opus-1 shape; its start-failure test (lines 49-50) calls start_supervised/1 and matches {{%KeyError{key: :mailer}, _stacktrace}, _child}, clean in itself. haiku-1 lines 34-35 start the default-named server in an async: true module, the shape 2026-10-21 graded violated, and line 46 assert {:error, _} = start_supervised(child) leaves the reason open, violated on "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason." as 2026-10-23 and this sweep's skill grade held. haiku-2 line 161 and sonnet-1 line 51 call start_link from a test. sonnet-2 is clean: every server is start_supervised! with a unique name (line 31), no start_link, no start-failure test. sonnet-1 line 22 passes name: nil through a custom child spec, so its servers are unnamed, which the rule allows.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" (unchanged): 5 of 5 violate. opus-1 (line 6 use ExUnit.Case, default async: false) and sonnet-1 (line 4) register the test process (opus-1 24, sonnet-1 21); haiku-2 (line 15) routes it through the application env (line 20); sonnet-2 (line 5) through :persistent_term (line 28). haiku-1 is the first baseline run in this case with async: true (line 17), but its double reads the application env (lines 11, 24) and one test starts the default-named server (lines 34-35), the global state the rule names, so the module runs concurrently while sharing it.

"Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours", "Use setup for shared data" and "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" (unchanged) are clean in 5 of 5: every double is a module with @behaviour Notify.Mailer passed as :mailer (haiku-2's reads its return value from the application env, which the concurrency rule counts); every setup returns a map matched in test heads (haiku-2 also matches pid at line 83); no test module has a @moduledoc, and use / alias (haiku-1 use / import / alias) open each body.

Outside the list: sonnet-1 lines 40-42 (cond do / fun.() -> :ok / attempts == 0 -> flunk("condition not met in time") / true ->) break "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line" ("`cond` already carries an expression on the left of each `->`, so its bodies go on the next line unless every one is a short literal or name", and "when one clause breaks, every clause of that `case` does") and fail mix format --check-formatted, recorded under "Before you finish" as well; no session ran mix format. The formatter wraps after == with the expected list on one line (opus-1 93-94, sonnet-1 72-73, sonnet-2 77-78) are not counted under "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call", as 2026-10-31-check held. Test support modules without @moduledoc (sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 TestMailer), private helpers above the tests (sonnet-1, sonnet-2), haiku-2's 99-character comment at line 70, which mix format leaves, and sonnet-2's helper name nil_name for a function that returns a unique atom are not counted. No captures in any file.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), ten times each: every run passed every time with no warnings or other output (opus-1 25 tests, haiku-1 18, haiku-2 14, sonnet-1 19, sonnet-2 21). mix format --check-formatted passes on opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 and fails on sonnet-1 (lines 40-41), confirming format_ok in result.json. Against 2026-10-23 (baseline): Run concurrently 5 as 5; Group tests 5 from 4 (opus-1 now violated by the new sentence); Assert with patterns 4 as 4 (haiku-1 now violated, sonnet-1 now clean); Wait 5 as 5; Start 4 as 4 (haiku-2 now violated, sonnet-2 now clean); Replace, Setup and Open 0 as 0.
